verdict.line: You lose if you let his Rage bar cap and eat a Mega Gnar all-in; you win if you poke him down and force every trade before level 6.

brief.thesis: Gnar's entire kit is gated by his passive Rage Gene — in mini form he's just a long-range poke-and-slow threat, but once his Rage meter fills he transforms into Mega Gnar and gains a hard-hitting area stun on W (Wallop) and a wall-stun ultimate on R (GNAR!). Jayce's whole plan is to dictate when that transformation happens: punish mini Gnar hard with ranged Cannon Stance poke and Hammer Stance dives, and simply disengage the instant his bar is near full.

theirWindow.what: He's one ability away from Mega Gnar, which adds an area stun on W (Wallop) and a wall-stun on R (GNAR!) once it's off its 90/60/30/0/0s cooldown. Do not commit a Hammer Stance Q (To the Skies!) leap or stand near a wall right as his bar caps.

yourWindow.when: His Q and E both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With Boomerang Throw (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) and Hop (22/19.5/17/14.5/12s) both down, Gnar has no poke, slow, or escape. Swap to Hammer Stance and all-in with E (Thundering Blow) into Q (To the Skies!) before either comes back up.

start.why: The 49.4% win rate start over 267 games gives you the sustain and AD to win early auto trades while Gnar is still in his fragile mini form.

boots.why: At 53% win rate over 115 games, Steelcaps blunt both Gnar's Hyper-empowered autos in mini form and Mega Gnar's physical burst on W (Wallop) and R (GNAR!).

core.why: Builds mana for Muramana scaling and fuels constant Lightning Field (W) procs to keep poking Gnar down as OP.GG's own tip recommends.
The active haste lets you re-engage faster than Gnar's long Hop and Boomerang cooldowns can reset, denying him safe disengages.
Mana-charged autos and abilities massively raise your burst ceiling for punishing his mini-form cooldown gaps.
The 22.4%-picked, 55.6% win-rate finisher on this path adds the dash-reset burst needed to close out a trade before he can Hop away.

runes.keystoneWhy: This is a melee-trade matchup where you're walking into range on Hammer Stance repeatedly — Conqueror's stacking damage and healing offsets his poke over extended fights, and it's the higher-win-rate page (53.3% over Sorcery's 46.8%).

summoners.why: Ignite is run on 52.7% of games at a 49.2% pick rate and lets you close out solo kills on mini Gnar before he reaches level 6 and Mega Gnar access — the Flash+Teleport split is only worth it if you're planning to play a scaling/siege lane instead.

playing.title: Track his Rage bar
playing.detail: Watch Gnar's Rage meter at all times — once it's near full he'll transform into Mega Gnar on his next ability use and gain the area-stunning W (Wallop). Don't commit a Hammer Stance Q (To the Skies!) leap right as he's about to pop.

playing.title: Poke in Cannon Stance
playing.detail: Use Cannon Stance Q (Shock Blast) at its 600 range to chip his mini form from safety. This is exactly the constant-pressure play OP.GG recommends, without exposing you to his longer 1100-range Boomerang Throw.

playing.title: Dive before level 6
playing.detail: Gnar has no ultimate until level 6, so levels 1-5 are your best all-in window — chain Hammer Stance E (Thundering Blow) into Q (To the Skies!) while he has zero access to Mega Gnar.

playing.title: Never engage a full Rage bar
playing.detail: Per OP.GG's own read, don't force a fight into Mega Gnar — his W (Wallop) stuns in an area and his R (GNAR!) stuns you against a wall for bonus damage. Disengage and wait for him to revert.

playing.title: Punish his landing after Hop
playing.detail: Gnar's E (Hop) leaps him onto you to bounce off your head for extra range. The instant he lands, hit Hammer Stance E (Thundering Blow) to knock him back and deny the second bounce.

playing.title: Punish a missed Boomerang catch
playing.detail: Boomerang Throw sits on a 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown unless he catches it on return. If you see him whiff the catch, his only poke and slow tool is down for a long stretch — shove the wave or trade freely.

playing.title: Build to re-engage, not to siege
playing.detail: Rush Tear of the Goddess into Youmuu's Ghostblade, Muramana, and Voltaic Cyclosword so your haste and mana-scaled damage let you catch him again before his long cooldowns reset, turning this even lane into your snowball.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spell rates, and the 49.8% head-to-head win rate over 251 games are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch; the tactical reads on Rage timing, stance swaps, and trade windows are my own judgment.
